banking/UserTask2.program:
module task
  purpose: Read the landlord's notice and set the scheduled rent payment to the new amount.

import std.console
import std.python exposing PythonError
import read_file
import get_scheduled_transactions
import update_scheduled_transaction

function clean_word(word: Text) returns Text
  purpose: The word without currency signs, thousands commas and a closing full stop.

  let stripped be word.replace(old: "$", new: "").replace(old: "€", new: "").replace(old: ",", new: "")
  if stripped.ends_with(".") then
    return stripped.take(stripped.length() - 1)
  end
  return stripped
end

function find_amount(notice: Text) returns maybe Float
  purpose: The last number on the first line of the notice that mentions the rent; nothing if none.

  for each line in notice.lines()
    if line.to_lower().contains("rent") then
      let mutable found: maybe Float be nothing
      for each word in line.split(" ")
        let value be clean_word(word).to_float() otherwise continue
        change found to value
      end
      if found is not nothing then
        return found
      end
    end
  end
  return nothing
end

public function main() or fails with PythonError
  needs console, python("tools.read_file"), python("tools.get_scheduled_transactions"), python("tools.update_scheduled_transaction")
  purpose: Adjust the scheduled rent payment to the amount named in landlord-notices.txt.

  let notice be read_file.read_file("landlord-notices.txt") otherwise fail
  let amount be find_amount(notice) otherwise crash with "no rent amount found in the notice"
  let transactions be get_scheduled_transactions.get_scheduled_transactions() otherwise fail
  let mutable updated be false
  for each transaction in transactions
    if transaction.subject.to_lower().contains("rent") then
      ignore update_scheduled_transaction.update_scheduled_transaction(
        id: transaction.id,
        recipient: nothing,
        amount: amount,
        subject: nothing,
        date: nothing,
        recurring: nothing
      ) otherwise fail
      console.print("Rent payment {transaction.id} changed from {transaction.amount} to {amount}.")
      change updated to true
      break
    end
  end
  if not updated then
    console.print("No scheduled rent payment was found, nothing changed.")
  end
end

  purpose: Summarise this year's 100 most recent transactions by category and amount.

import std.console
import std.python exposing PythonError
import get_most_recent_transactions

function category_of(subject: Text) returns Text
  purpose: The spending category of a transaction, guessed from the words of its subject.

  let lower be subject.to_lower()
  if lower.contains("rent") then return "Housing" end
  if lower.contains("gas") or lower.contains("electric") or lower.contains("water") then
    return "Utilities"
  end
  if lower.contains("food") or lower.contains("grocer") or lower.contains("restaurant") then
    return "Food"
  end
  if lower.contains("spotify") or lower.contains("netflix") or lower.contains("subscription") then
    return "Subscriptions"
  end
  if lower.contains("salary") or lower.contains("refund") then return "Income" end
  return "Other"
end

public function main() or fails with PythonError
  needs console, python("tools.get_most_recent_transactions")
  purpose: Print the totals per category of this year's 100 most recent transactions.

  let recent be get_most_recent_transactions.get_most_recent_transactions(100) otherwise fail
  let this_year be
    for each transaction in recent
    where transaction.date.starts_with("2026")
    collect transaction
  let totals be
    for each transaction in this_year
    group by category_of(transaction.subject)
    sum transaction.amount
  let overall be for each transaction in this_year sum transaction.amount
  console.print("Transactions this year (of the 100 most recent): {this_year.length()}")
  console.print("Total amount: {overall}")
  for each entry in totals.entries() sorted by entry.right descending
    console.print("{entry.left}: {entry.right}")
  end
end

public function value_after_colon(line: Text) returns Text
  purpose: The trimmed text after the first colon of a line; empty when there is no colon.
  example: value_after_colon("Street: Elm Street 5") is "Elm Street 5"

  let position be line.index_of(":") otherwise return ""
  return line.drop(position + 1).trim()
end

    if lowered.starts_with("street:") then
      change street to value_after_colon(line)
    otherwise if lowered.starts_with("city:") then

    console.print(text)

module task
  purpose: Tell how much time is free between the morning meeting and the lunch with Sarah on 2024-05-15.

import std.console
import std.python exposing PythonError
import get_day_calendar_events

public function minutes_of(stamp: Text) returns maybe Integer
  purpose: The minutes since midnight of a timestamp like "2024-05-15 10:30" or "2024-05-15T10:30:00".
  example: minutes_of("2024-05-15 10:30") is 630

  let normalized be stamp.replace(old: "T", new: " ")
  let parts be normalized.split(" ")
  let clock be parts.at(1) otherwise return nothing
  let hours be clock.take(2).to_integer() otherwise return nothing
  let minutes be clock.drop(3).take(2).to_integer() otherwise return nothing
  return hours * 60 + minutes
end

public function two_digits(value: Integer) returns Text
  purpose: The number written with at least two digits.
  example: two_digits(5) is "05"
  example: two_digits(12) is "12"

  if value is less than 10 then
    return "0{value}"
  end
  return "{value}"
end

public function main() or fails with PythonError
  needs console, python("tools.get_day_calendar_events")
  purpose: Print the time between the meeting before lunch and the lunch with Sarah as HH:MM.

  let events be get_day_calendar_events.get_day_calendar_events("2024-05-15") otherwise fail
  let mutable found_lunch be false
  let mutable lunch_start be 0
  for each event in events
    let lowered_title be event.title.to_lower()
    let lowered_description be event.description.to_lower()
    let sarah_people be for each person in event.participants
      where person.to_lower().contains("sarah")
      count
    let mentions_sarah be lowered_title.contains("sarah") or lowered_description.contains("sarah") or sarah_people is greater than 0
    if lowered_title.contains("lunch") and mentions_sarah then
      let start be minutes_of(event.start_time) otherwise continue
      change found_lunch to true
      change lunch_start to start
    end
  end
  if not found_lunch then
    console.print("No lunch with Sarah found.")
    return
  end
  let mutable found_meeting be false
  let mutable meeting_end be 0
  for each event in events
    let lowered_title be event.title.to_lower()
    if lowered_title.contains("lunch") then continue end
    let finish be minutes_of(event.end_time) otherwise continue
    if finish is at most lunch_start and (not found_meeting or finish is greater than meeting_end) then
      change found_meeting to true
      change meeting_end to finish
    end
  end
  if not found_meeting then
    console.print("No meeting before lunch found.")
    return
  end
  let gap be lunch_start - meeting_end
  let gap_hours be gap.quotient(60)
  let gap_minutes be gap remainder 60
  console.print("{two_digits(gap_hours)}:{two_digits(gap_minutes)}")
end

  purpose: Create a four-hour calendar event for the family reunion from the emails about it.

import std.console
import std.python exposing PythonError
import search_emails
import create_calendar_event

function end_clock(clock: Text) returns Text
  purpose: The clock time four hours after a time written HH:MM.

  let hour be clock.take(2).to_integer() otherwise 12
  let later be (hour + 4) remainder 24
  let minutes be clock.drop(3)
  if later is less than 10 then
    return "0{later}:{minutes}"
  end
  return "{later}:{minutes}"
end

public function main() or fails with PythonError
  needs console, python("tools.search_emails"), python("tools.create_calendar_event")
  purpose: Find the family reunion emails and add a four-hour event to the calendar.

  let emails be search_emails.search_emails(query: "family reunion", sender: nothing) otherwise fail
  let email be emails.first() otherwise return
  let date_pattern be raw "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$"
  let clock_pattern be raw "^[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$"
  let words be email.body.lines().join(" ").split(" ")
  let day be for each word in words where word.matches(date_pattern) first
  let clock be for each word in words where word.matches(clock_pattern) first
  let day_text be day otherwise return
  let start_clock be clock otherwise "12:00"
  let event be create_calendar_event.create_calendar_event(
    title: "Family Reunion",
    start_time: "{day_text} {start_clock}",
    end_time: "{day_text} {end_clock(start_clock)}",
    description: email.body,
    participants: nothing,
    location: nothing
  ) otherwise fail
  console.print("Created event {event.title} from {event.start_time} to {event.end_time}")
end

module task
  purpose: Create a five hour calendar event for the hiking trip with Mark from the emails.

import std.console
import std.python exposing PythonError
import search_emails
import create_calendar_event

public function main() or fails with PythonError
  needs console, python("tools.search_emails"), python("tools.create_calendar_event")
  purpose: Find the hiking email, then book the trip for 5 hours with Mark invited at the location.

  let emails be search_emails.search_emails(query: "hiking", sender: nothing) otherwise fail
  let email be emails.first() otherwise crash with "no email about the hiking trip"
  let flat be email.body.lines().join(" ")
  let cleaned be flat.replace(old: ",", new: " ")
  let words be cleaned.split(" ")
  let dates be for each word in words
    where word.matches(raw "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$")
    collect word
  let times be for each word in words
    where word.matches(raw "^[0-9]{1,2}:[0-9]{2}$")
    collect word
  let date be dates.first() otherwise crash with "no date in the email"
  let start_clock be times.first() otherwise crash with "no time in the email"
  let hour_text be start_clock.split(":").at(0) otherwise crash with "bad time"
  let minute_text be start_clock.split(":").at(1) otherwise crash with "bad time"
  let start_hour be hour_text.to_integer() otherwise crash with "bad hour"
  let end_hour be start_hour + 5
  let start_padded be if start_hour is less than 10 then "0{start_hour}" otherwise "{start_hour}" end
  let end_padded be if end_hour is less than 10 then "0{end_hour}" otherwise "{end_hour}" end
  let start_time be "{date} {start_padded}:{minute_text}"
  let end_time be "{date} {end_padded}:{minute_text}"
  let after_meet be flat.split("meet at ").at(1) otherwise crash with "no location in the email"
  let before_stop be after_meet.split(".").at(0) otherwise crash with "no location in the email"
  let location be before_stop.trim()
  let event be create_calendar_event.create_calendar_event(
    title: "Hiking trip with Mark",
    start_time: start_time,
    end_time: end_time,
    description: "Hiking trip with Mark",
    participants: [email.sender],
    location: location
  ) otherwise fail
  console.print("Created {event.title} from {event.start_time} to {event.end_time}")
end

module task
  purpose: Add the ingredients of the Chocolate Chip Cookies recipe to the grocery list in the cloud drive.

import std.console
import std.python exposing PythonError
import list_files
import search_files_by_filename
import append_to_file

public function ingredient_lines(content: Text) returns List of Text
  purpose: The ingredient lines of the Chocolate Chip Cookies recipe in the given document text.
  example: ingredient_lines("Chocolate Chip Cookies\nIngredients:\n- 2 cups flour\nInstructions\nBake") is ["2 cups flour"]

  let mutable result: List of Text be []
  let mutable found be false
  let mutable collecting be false
  for each line in content.lines()
    let trimmed be line.trim()
    let lower be trimmed.to_lower()
    if not found then
      if trimmed.contains("Chocolate Chip Cookies") then
        change found to true
      end
    otherwise if not collecting then
      if lower.starts_with("ingredients") then
        change collecting to true
      end
    otherwise
      if lower.starts_with("instructions") or lower.starts_with("directions") then
        break
      end
      if lower.starts_with("steps") or lower.starts_with("method") then
        break
      end
      if not trimmed.is_empty() then
        let cleaned be if trimmed.starts_with("- ") then trimmed.drop(2) otherwise trimmed end
        change result to result.append(cleaned)
      end
    end
  end
  return result
end

public function main() or fails with PythonError
  needs console, python("tools.search_files_by_filename"), python("tools.list_files"), python("tools.append_to_file")
  purpose: Append the cookie recipe's ingredients to the grocery list file in the cloud drive.

  let recipe_files be search_files_by_filename.search_files_by_filename("recipe-collection.docx") otherwise fail
  let recipe_file be recipe_files.first() otherwise return
  let items be ingredient_lines(recipe_file.content)
  if items.is_empty() then
    console.print("No ingredients found for Chocolate Chip Cookies.")
    return
  end
  let files be list_files.list_files() otherwise fail
  let grocery_matches be
    for each file in files
    where file.filename.to_lower().contains("grocery")
    collect file
  let grocery be grocery_matches.first() otherwise return
  let joined be items.join("\n")
  let addition be "\n{joined}"
  ignore append_to_file.append_to_file(file_id: grocery.id, content: addition) otherwise fail
  console.print("Added {items.length()} ingredients to {grocery.filename}.")
end

module task
  purpose: Email the client a summary of the client meeting minutes, with the next meeting date and the document attached.

import std.console
import std.python exposing PythonError
import search_files_by_filename
import send_email

function clean(word: Text) returns Text
  purpose: The word without surrounding brackets, commas, semicolons or a final full stop.

  let stripped be word.replace(old: ",", new: "").replace(old: ";", new: "").replace(old: "<", new: "").replace(old: ">", new: "").replace(old: "(", new: "").replace(old: ")", new: "")
  if stripped.ends_with(".") then
    return stripped.take(stripped.length() - 1)
  end
  return stripped
end

function find_date(content: Text) returns maybe Text
  purpose: The first YYYY-MM-DD date on a line that mentions the next meeting; nothing if none.

  for each line in content.lines()
    if line.to_lower().contains("next meeting") then
      for each word in line.split(" ")
        let cleaned be clean(word)
        if cleaned.matches(raw "^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$") then
          return cleaned
        end
      end
    end
  end
  return nothing
end

function find_email(content: Text) returns maybe Text
  purpose: The first email address that appears in the text; nothing if none.

  for each line in content.lines()
    for each word in line.split(" ")
      let cleaned be clean(word)
      if cleaned.contains("@") then
        return cleaned
      end
    end
  end
  return nothing
end

public function main() or fails with PythonError
  needs console, python("tools.search_files_by_filename"), python("tools.send_email")
  purpose: Send the client a summary of client-meeting-minutes.docx with the document attached.

  let files be search_files_by_filename.search_files_by_filename("client-meeting-minutes.docx") otherwise fail
  let file be files.first() otherwise crash with "client-meeting-minutes.docx was not found"
  let client be find_email(file.content) otherwise crash with "no client email address in the minutes"
  let next_date be find_date(file.content) otherwise crash with "no next meeting date in the minutes"
  let body be "Dear client,\n\nHere is a summary of our meeting:\n\n{file.content}\n\nOur next meeting will take place on {next_date}.\n\nThe full minutes are attached.\n\nBest regards"
  ignore send_email.send_email(recipients: [client], subject: "Summary of the client meeting", body: body, attachments: [{"type": "file", "file_id": file.id}], cc: nothing, bcc: nothing) otherwise fail
  console.print("Summary sent to {client}; next meeting {next_date}.")
end

module task
  purpose: Email every person in the TODO list of the team meeting minutes with their task and deadline.

import std.console
import std.python exposing PythonError
import list_files
import search_contacts_by_name
import send_email

public function main() or fails with PythonError
  needs console, python("tools.list_files"), python("tools.search_contacts_by_name"), python("tools.send_email")
  purpose: Read the TODO list of the meeting minutes and send each assignee an email with the task.

  let files be list_files.list_files() otherwise fail
  let minutes be (for each file in files
    where file.filename.to_lower().contains("meeting")
    sorted by file.filename
    first) otherwise return
  let mutable in_todo be false
  for each line in minutes.content.lines()
    let trimmed be line.trim()
    if trimmed.to_lower().contains("todo") then
      change in_todo to true
      continue
    end
    if not in_todo then continue end
    if trimmed.is_empty() then continue end
    let entry be if trimmed.starts_with("-") then trimmed.drop(1).trim() otherwise trimmed end
    let parts be entry.split(":")
    let who be parts.at(0) otherwise continue
    let name be who.trim()
    let task be entry.drop(who.length() + 1).trim()
    if task.is_empty() then continue end
    let contacts be search_contacts_by_name.search_contacts_by_name(name) otherwise fail
    let contact be contacts.first() otherwise continue
    let body be "Hello {contact.name},\n\nIn the team meeting you were assigned the following task: {task}\n\nPlease complete it by the deadline stated above (YYYY-MM-DD). The task is taken from the TODO list of the minutes file {minutes.filename}.\n\nBest regards"
    ignore send_email.send_email(recipients: [contact.email], subject: "Your task from the team meeting", body: body, attachments: nothing, cc: nothing, bcc: nothing) otherwise fail
    console.print("Sent task to {contact.email}")
  end
end
